newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close slightly off in weak trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close slightly off in weak trade.

text.p: Brazil stocks ended lower in thin turnover on Monday, with major investors out of the market ahead of the mid-April futures index and options settlements, brokers said.
"Investors, particularly foreigners, traditionally prefer to be on the sidelines before the settlements because trading is more speculative than usual," one trader said.

The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares closed off 0.65 percent at 9,456 points. Market volume was lower at 352.1 million reais ($330.9 million), below the bolsa's recent average daily turnover of $500-$600 million.
The futures index contracts will be liquidated Wednesday, while the options will settle on April 22.
Traders said the Brazilian bolsa opened lower, still reflecting Wall Street's sharp losses on Friday. However, local share prices failed to follow the Dow as it bounced back later in the day.
Bellwether Telebras preferred fell 0.26 percent to 117 reais, while its common stock lost 0.97 percent to 112.30 reais.
State mining concern Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) dropped 0.98 percent to 25.15 reais.
Other big losers among the blue-chips were federal power reais and state oil firm Petrobras which lost 0.23 percent to 209.50 reais.
Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, lost 1.9 percent, closing at 2,603 points.
